extracted.intended_audience: United States Indian agents and Indian Bureau officials (agency superintendents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative dimensions for preparing and assessing United States Indian agency annual reports (circa 1880), covering agency condition, population, agriculture, schools, policing, infrastructure, and social indicators. Used to judge progress in 'civilization' and management of reservations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report clarity and conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: The report should furnish this office with a clear, concise view of your (my) agency, the condition, habits, and disposition of the Indians under your (my) care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include such information as to afford to one who inquires for the first time respecting your (my) Indians a fair picture of their condition and a condensed history of the year's work. (Text: circular of July 18)

rubrics_metrics.name: Population and location statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide precise counts and locations of Indians under charge: numbers on reservations, off-reservation populations, and distribution by tribes/bands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give totals and breakdowns (e.g., 'Of the 3,503 Indians under my charge, 1,748 are living upon the reservations assigned them' and list where those living off-reservation are located).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural acreage and improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Report acres under cultivation, acres fenced, new acres broken, acres of particular crops and improvements to farms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statistics such as acres under fence, acres cultivated (e.g., '1,248 acres under cultivation'), new broken land (e.g., '1,000 acres have been broken'), miles/rods of fencing, diking, ditching, and notes on crop yields per acre and causes of shortfall (seed shortages, use of former crops for subsistence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crop production quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify agricultural output by crop (bushels of wheat, oats, corn, potatoes; tons of hay; vegetables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give estimated totals (e.g., 'wheat 18,000 bushels; oats 17,000 bushels; corn 500 bushels; potatoes 3,000 bushels; 100 tons of hay') and note marketability of surplus and seasonal factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Farming implements, wagons, and mechanization
rubrics_metrics.description: Record purchases and possession of farm equipment, wagons, reapers, threshers, and intention to mechanize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List numbers and cost where possible (e.g., 'purchased 45 farm wagons, increasing to 60; cost over $7,000'), and note plans to buy reaper and threshing machine as indicators of agricultural advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial habits and home improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of improving industrial habits: building houses, stables, fences, lumber use, shingle production, sawed lumber, and construction of new buildings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe types of construction (log, squared logs, sawed lumber), sawmill outputs (e.g., '60,000 feet of lumber'), manufactured goods sold (e.g., '400,000 shingles manufactured and some sold to whites') and how proceeds are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and operation of trading-posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and adequacy of trading-posts on the agency and their effect on local trade and liquor procurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether a trading-post exists, whether it draws in a suitable occupant, and effects of its absence (Indians going to settlements, procurement of whisky, neglect of farms).

rubrics_metrics.name: School and mission operations and capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Report existence, enrollment, progress, and accommodation of schools/industrial boarding-schools and missions, and capacity/need for expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record number of scholars, average attendance, instruction offered (English, household duties, manual labor), building additions, and recommendations for funding to expand to target enrollment (e.g., recommendation to provide for 100 pupils at Puyallup).

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational outcomes and vocational training
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe scholastic proficiency, manual skill training, and the reflex influence of schools on adult behavior and employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examination results (comparative statements such as 'would have been creditable to white children'), evidence of more systematic housekeeping and farming among pupils who left school, and apprentices placed in shops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health and sanitary conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on sanitary state, disease incidence, physician activity, number treated, deaths, and births.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts (e.g., '654 cases treated; 27 deaths; 32 births'), note measures taken by the physician (village cleanliness, decreasing reliance on traditional 'medicinemen'), and effects of weather on sickness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime, justice, and policing
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe crime incidence, functioning of Indian police and councils, methods of trial, appeals, and notable criminal cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report that crime has decreased, layout the role of elected head-men boards trying petty cases, the police trying criminal cases with appeal to agent, and specific incidents (murders, imprisonments awaiting trial). Recommend reorganization or appointment of energetic white man if police inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian police effectiveness and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess police performance, recruitment difficulties, demoralizing effects of disturbances, and recommendations for structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note inability to induce best Indians to accept positions, recommend appointment of at least one energetic white man for special duty if reorganization is not advisable at present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship and vocational uptake
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure uptake of apprenticeships, willingness of young men to learn mechanical trades, and barriers (disinclination to confinement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report number apprenticed (e.g., 'Four apprentices'), their origins (formerly in school), observed aptitude in shops, and note inability to compel adoption of apprentice system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel, stock, and external trespass impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Record effects of stock and freighting travel on reserves (forage destruction) and enforcement actions taken against trespassers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note complaints, reporting offenders to district attorney, and whether effective prevention has been achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lands in severalty / homesteading obstacles
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on efforts to induce Indians to accept lands in severalty/homesteads and obstacles such as desire to keep tribal relations and inability/unwillingness to pay commissions/fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend relieving payment requirements to encourage homesteading; report consultations and Indians' reluctance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure and government buildings need
rubrics_metrics.description: Document need for agency buildings, hospitals, barns, school buildings, and other government structures and record appropriations or lack thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that buildings are imperative, record new constructions (boarding-school additions, shops, hospital), note climate-driven maintenance needs and history of no appropriations for agency buildings for twenty years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land reclamation and drainage works
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on diking, ditching, tide gates and other reclamation works that redeem tide flats or swampy lands for agricultural use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measures constructed (e.g., '226 rods of diking and two tide gates, 120 rods of post and rail fencing') and expected acreage made fit for cultivation (e.g., 'redeem about 70 acres of rich tide flats').

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic/self-support potential of agency projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether school farms, reclamation, and improved agriculture can render institutions self-supporting and increase Indians' market participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use production figures and planned works to estimate self-sufficiency (e.g., Puyallup school farm improvements to make school self-supporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious and mission influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Note presence, activity, and influence of mission bodies (Presbyterian, Jesuit, Sisters of Charity) on spiritual welfare, education, and moral advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe missionary work, buildings erected (churches), and credit given to Fathers and Sisters for patient devotion and educational effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of 'progressive civilization'
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative indicators such as adoption of citizens' dress, desire for houses and furniture, inclination to educate children, and following advice of agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide observational commentary on change in habits and manners compared to former condition; cite conduct during excitements as evidence of progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market access and sale of surplus produce
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on ability to sell surplus farm produce (local markets, transport methods) and price differences relative to settlers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note means of transport (packing on animals, lake flat-boats), proximity to markets (towns, New Tacoma), and statements such as 'find a ready sale at good prices' and reasons (seasonal road conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of external economic opportunities (sealing, freighting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for seasonal/alternative income sources (seal-hunting, freighting) and their effect on farming participation and savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report amounts earned by such activities (e.g., 'about $20,060 was distributed among the two tribes' from sealing) and note that such opportunities may reduce farming labor or provide winter savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of births, deaths, and medical trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep civil vital statistics and report Indians' changing trust from 'medicinemen' to government physician.

rubrics_metrics.name: (fragmented textual indicators handled)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture and report incomplete or interrupted observations verbatim when context is broken in the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the source text is broken or hyphenated across lines (typical of scanned 1880 reports), preserve the original phrasing as far as possible and annotate where sentences continue on other pages.
